candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether more-stringent Section 405(d)(2) criteria or unlisted pollutants are treated as superseding permit limits affects which numeric limits and monitoring obligations are considered applicable versus permit-stated values.

candidates.exact_span: If new limits for Molybdenum are promulgated prior to permit expiration, then those limits shall become directly enforceable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether promulgated molybdenum limits are deemed in effect before permit expiration determines whether an enforceable numeric limit exists for molybdenum compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a planned change in sludge disposal practice triggers different or additional permit conditions affects which limits and monitoring requirements are treated as operative for the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the one-time, within-one-year TCLP testing window determines whether TCLP monitoring was required during Federal FY2025 and how absent TCLP results are classified (required-but-missing versus not yet due or not required).

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sampling must occur after final treatment and before off-site transfer affects which events count as required monitoring and whether missing results reflect a documented no-test state or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as hazardous waste shifts the governing compliance framework from Table 1 land-application limits to RCRA disposal standards and associated monitoring or handling obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this prohibition is treated as an enforceable compliance standard affects whether disposal-path evidence is evaluated against a binding restriction rather than only numeric pollutant concentrations.

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a TCLP failure triggers a 24-hour notification obligation affects monitoring/reporting requirement applicability and how documented failure or missing notification is categorized.

candidates.exact_span: A written rep ort shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the seven-day written-report duty after TCLP failure affects whether reporting was required and whether missing reports indicate inadequate evidence versus a documented no-failure state.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall not be applied to the land if the concentration of the pollutants exceeds the pollutant concentration criteria in Table 1.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This ties land-application eligibility to Table 1 pollutant concentration criteria; different readings of which pollutants are covered or how exceedance is measured change applicable numeric limits and compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of testing for pollutants in Table 1 is found in Element 1, Section I.C.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of Table 1 pollutant testing depends on the externally referenced frequency schedule; unresolved cross-reference interpretation changes which monitoring intervals were required and how missing Table 1 results are classified.
